questions.explanation: The trap is: Plates lurch in sudden jolts, snapping into new positions. Scene s4 shows why this is wrong: Plates creep, they never lurch: about two centimetres a year, slower than your fingernails grow.

questions.explanation: Scene s3: where the plates meet, the denser plate is forced down and slides underneath the other - that sinking is called subduction.
questions.prompt: Two plates push together and meet head-on. What happens next to the denser plate?

questions.answer: They are called plates. Year after year they drift - the two plates in the animation sit apart at first and slowly drift towards each other.
questions.explanation: Scene s1: the Earth's crust is made of giant slabs of rock called plates, and year after year they drift towards each other.
questions.prompt: What are the giant slabs of rock that make up the Earth's crust called, and what do they do year after year?

questions.answer: Subduction is when one plate sinks and slides under another plate where they meet. It happens to the denser plate, which is forced down underneath the lighter plate.
questions.explanation: Scene s3: subduction is the sinking of the denser plate under the other plate where the two collide.
questions.prompt: In your own words, say what subduction means and which plate it happens to.
